no45.summary: The Conde de Miranda, at Naples, to the Duque de Feria, in the Spanish syllabic cipher of 1592-93: advice on a confidant to be used 'con este achaque', a business 'a costa de la bolsa', and a request that a person be chosen through whom he can be written to without it being understood.

no79.summary: The Duque de Sessa, at Rome, to Diego de Ibarra, wholly in cipher: 'de ver los testemonios que a todos levantan ... los que bivimos en Roma', the election and 'diversas pretensiones', 'no puedo dexar de hazerlo, a lo menos, de que no esten ministros conformes'. Read line by line with the office key (BnF fr. 3995 f. 97); unresolved groups marked.
no79.en:

no47.summary: A copy of Sessa's despatch to Philip II, with the beginning of a contemporary decipherment written above the cipher lines in lighter ink ('por via de mar ... difiriendo de dia en dia'); read with the office key, which agrees with the gloss wherever both survive.
no47.en:
On the 30th of last month, by a courier of my own, I informed Your Majesty at length of everything that was offered
here in particular on the affair of France, of which [I have] sent duplicate couriers by sea and land; and the despatch
has gone on being put off from day to day, another courier to Your Majesty, waiting to see whether some certain news
would come from Paris, from where the [∂ir] to Your Majesty a fresh letter with which I find myself of the [hir] of Your
Majesty; it is from don Diego de […] […] […], of 28 April, with a copy of what he wrote to Your Majesty; and I also know
that […] […] [xir] that he has had no letters from the legate for many days, and I believe without doubt that the
couriers must be getting lost.

snip.cap: BnF Français 3995 f. 97: the Spanish office key, the letter alphabet across the top and the syllable table beneath, identical to Tomokiyo’s reconstruction
snip.credit: Bibliothèque nationale de France, fr. 3995 f. 97, via Gallica

system: Spanish office cipher of 1592-93: two-digit numbers carry consonant-vowel syllables, a small homophonic symbol alphabet carries bare letters, diacritics add a final consonant, and two- and three-letter groups carry the nomenclature.
